headline_marked: Nearly 300 [[detained in raid on JaSaD office]] in Dhaka
headline: Nearly 300 detained in raid on JaSaD office in Dhaka
summary: Police raided the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal headquarters in Gulistan, citing suspected Awami League activities and potential sabotage.
details: Police detained nearly 300 people following a raid on the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD) headquarters in Dhaka’s Gulistan area on Saturday.
Motijheel Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Harun-or-Rashid stated that approximately 280 to 300 individuals were taken into custody and moved to Paltan Police Station in handcuffs.

Authorities claimed the raid was based on information that activists of the Awami League, which is currently banned from political activities, had gathered to carry out sabotage or other unlawful activities.
Police also reported receiving information that  ‘Joy Bangla’ slogans were were sounded at the office, which further prompted the action.

Former Dhaka Union of Journalists President Abu Jafar Surya was among those detained. He claimed via Facebook that he was performing professional duties at a representatives’ meeting when he was arrested.
JaSaD Office Secretary Sazzad Hossain rejected the allegations of a secret Awami League meeting, calling them ‘false’.
Hossain further alleged that BNP and Jatiotabadi Jubo Dal activists had attacked their meeting before police intervened and detained the members.
Deputy Commissioner Harun-or-Rashid confirmed that authorities are verifying the identities and activities of those detained, and those found involved in unlawful acts will face legal action.

headline_marked: 4 arrested as [[Mirpur health centre demolished]] and looted
headline: 4 arrested as Mirpur health centre demolished and looted
summary: Over 200 masked attackers used heavy machinery to raze the Radda MCH-FP Center, destroying vaccines and medical equipment worth over ৳1.5 crore.
details: Over 200 masked attackers armed with local weapons stormed the Radda MCH-FP Center in Mirpur around midnight last Thursday. The attackers held security guards hostage and looted medical equipment, medicines, and vaccines before using heavy machinery to demolish the facility.

The facility's Executive Director, Nasrin Akhtar, reported losses exceeding ৳1 crore, while other reports indicate equipment and vaccines worth ৳1.5 crore were destroyed or stolen. A case was filed at Shah Ali Police Station, leading to the arrest of four suspects.

The Democratic Rights Committee has condemned the attack, calling it a 'terrorist attack' on the public's right to live. They highlighted that the demolition occurred during a measles and dengue epidemic, destroying critical government vaccination records and vaccines.

The committee alleged that the attack was a planned land-grabbing attempt carried out under political patronage, claiming a local BNP leader, Hanif Mia, was involved. They further alleged that the demolition took place while police were present at the scene.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) commissioner has ordered a probe into police negligence during the overnight demolition. A three-member body has been formed to investigate the role of the police in the attack.
The Democratic Rights Committee is demanding the immediate arrest of the masterminds and the reconstruction of the clinic to restore essential health services for poor mothers and children.
